Modality type: classification of data representation forms a retrieval system handles — text, image, table, code, audio, video, or structured data.
Multi-modal embedding model: neural network architecture that projects content from different modalities into a shared vector space enabling cross-modal similarity search.
Cross-modal retrieval: searching for content in one modality using a query from a different modality, such as retrieving images from a text query or code from a table context.

Modal fusion strategy: mechanism for combining or harmonizing representations from multiple modalities — early fusion (embedding-level concatenation), late fusion (score-level aggregation), or intermediate fusion (attention-based cross-modal interaction).

Non-text chunk processor: component that parses, extracts, and encodes non-text content from documents — handling image pixels, table cells, code syntax, or audio waveforms into retrievable representations.
Table extraction: parsing structured tabular data from documents or PDFs into machine-readable format with row/column headers preserved for retrieval and reasoning.
Image/figure extraction: isolating visual elements from documents — charts, diagrams, photographs — for separate encoding and retrieval alongside text.
Code chunk handler: processing code snippets with language-aware parsing to capture syntax, imports, function signatures, and docstrings as retrieval units.
Multi-modal index: index structure supporting heterogeneous chunk types — text vectors, image features, table embeddings — with metadata routing for modality-aware retrieval.
Modality-specific retriever: specialized retrieval component tuned to a particular modality's retrieval patterns, scoring functions, and similarity measures.
Heterogeneous retrieval engine: unified retrieval layer that queries across mixed content types, resolving modality mismatches and ranking results from diverse sources.
Cross-modal similarity metric: distance or similarity measure applicable across modality boundaries — enabling comparison of text query vectors against image embeddings, for example.
Multi-modal reranker: post-retrieval component that reorders mixed-modality candidates using cross-attention between query and all retrieved content types.
Modality confidence scorer: scoring function estimating retrieval quality per modality, enabling fallback decisions when a modality's results are unreliable.
Multi-modal memory store: persistent storage holding retrieved chunks across modalities with indexing supporting mixed-modality queries and temporal session context.
Table-to-text generator: component converting retrieved tabular data into natural language summaries or explanations for injection into the generation prompt.
Image description encoder: vision model producing text-aligned representations of images — captions, scene graphs, or dense captions — enabling image content in text-based retrieval.
Scene graph extractor: parsing visual content into structured entity-relationship graphs capturing objects, attributes, and spatial relationships for graph-based retrieval.
Audio-video transcription: converting temporal media to text transcripts with timestamps, enabling retrieval of relevant segments by text query.
Document page segmenter: component that splits compound documents into modality-homogeneous chunks — separating text blocks from embedded figures and tables.
Multi-modal query router: routing layer classifying query type and directing retrieval toward appropriate modality-specific or cross-modal retrieval paths.
Visual question answering retriever: retrieving image regions or full images that answer visual queries, returning image crops plus textual annotations.
Code semantic embedder: embedding code snippets capturing functional semantics, API usage patterns, and documentation context for semantic code retrieval.
Modality alignment calibrator: training or fine-tuning procedure aligning embedding spaces across modalities using contrastive learning or shared latent representations.

Structured data retrieval: RAG variant that indexes and retrieves from structured sources — databases, JSON, knowledge graphs — alongside unstructured text, with query-to-SQL or query-to-SPARQL translation as a sub-component.
Temporal media segment retriever: retrieving specific time segments from audio or video based on query relevance, returning transcript snippets with start/end timestamps and modality metadata.
Multi-modal context builder: constructing the generation-augmenting context by assembling retrieved chunks of mixed types, handling format conversion and ordering for downstream generation.
RAG architecture decomposed into interchangeable components: retrievers, rerankers, routers, generators, and memory modules assembled per task

Reciprocal Rank Fusion — a rank-based fusion technique that combines multiple ranked retrieval lists by weighting each item by the reciprocal of its rank position (1/rank) and summing across all lists to produce a unified fused ranking.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion algorithm: combines multiple ranked retrieval lists into a unified ranking using the formula 1/(k+rank) where k is a constant hyperparameter
The union of all unique documents appearing in any contributing rank list; the fusion score is computed only for documents present in the candidate pool.

A positive smoothing constant (conventional value 60) added to each rank position before taking the reciprocal, preventing division by zero and dampening sensitivity to high ranks for stable fusion scoring
A single retrieval system (e.g., dense retriever, sparse BM25, keyword search) whose ranked output list participates in the fusion; RRF requires at least two contributing streams.
A document uniquely identified within the fusion process by its document_id, carrying accumulated scores from one or more retrieval systems and participating in the final sort
The merged document list produced by sorting all candidates in descending order by their fusion scores, yielding a unified cross-system ranking that reflects all input retrieval evidence
The scoring formula: RRF(d) = Σ 1/(k+rank_i(d)) summed over all retrieval systems i that return document d
The final unified ranking produced by sorting all candidate documents by their fusion scores in descending order; constitutes the output of the RRF process fed into downstream stages.
The sum of reciprocal rank values for a given document across all contributing rank lists; the document's position in the fused ranking is determined by descending fusion score.

A smoothing constant added to the rank position in the denominator to dampen the contribution of low-ranked items and reduce sensitivity to rank differences among poorly ranked results; standard value is 60.
Optional score normalization (min-max or z-score) applied to raw retrieval scores before rank extraction, improving fusion robustness when source systems use disparate scoring scales
An ordered sequence of documents or passage identifiers produced by a single retrieval system, where each item carries an integer rank position starting at 1 for the top-scoring item.
The integer position of an item within a rank list, starting at 1 for the highest-scoring result; used as the denominator in reciprocal rank computation.
An ordered sequence of document identifiers returned by a single retrieval system, ranked by that system's internal relevance scoring mechanism, where position encodes ordinal relevance

The value 1/(rank_position + k) where k is a smoothing constant (commonly k=60), computed per-item per-rank-list; items with higher ranks (lower position numbers) receive larger reciprocal rank values.
The per-system score for a document computed as 1 divided by the sum of rank position and constant k, yielding a value in (0, 1/k] that decays with worsening rank
One of the multiple retrieval subsystems (dense, sparse, keyword, or hybrid) that produces an independent ranked document list submitted to the fusion algorithm for combination

Optional pre-processing step applied to raw retrieval scores from each system before rank extraction, ensuring comparable score ranges across heterogeneous retrieval methods such as dense vector search and BM25.
Extended RRF variant introducing per-system weights multiplied by each reciprocal rank contribution, allowing differential credit for systems with varying reliability or relevance to the query type
The operation of combining per-system rank evidence into a single score via summation across systems
Optional pre-processing step applying min-max or z-score normalization to raw retrieval scores before fusion
